items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I remember playing a wedding pretty soon after I moved to New York with Buddy Tate on saxophone, Mel Lewis on drums and Steve Kuhn on piano.

ctx.x: Yeah. And then I wound up having to move out of that apartment. That’s a whole other story, well we don’t have to get into that story, but so anyway, so six months nothing. No work. I was ready to take a day job. I’d never worked, in fact I never have — knock on wood — never have done anything but music my whole life, since I was ten. So this was really depressing for me. And I actually talked my way into a job with a photo, one of these photo processing labs, Gene Berry Photos, as the Assistant Manager. And I…

items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I played in Loren Schoenberg’s band, a great guy who now is up at the Jazz Museum in Harlem. He had a wonderful big band. And we had kind of semi-regular gigs with that band. Mel Lewis was the drummer.

ctx.x: 1997. We had just sort of started doing these interview sessions and I remember that was, musically that was a great party. I wonder if you could do me a favor, for people who will watch this and if you can think back to 1997 or about then, what a typical, let’s say week or ten day period for you was like, employment/music-wise.

Yeah. That, you know the 80s and 90s were really interesting for me ‘cause there were a lot of different kinds of gigs that I did, everything from big bands, small groups, there were a lot of big bands still playing in New York. I played in Loren Schoenberg’s band, a great guy who now is up at the Jazz Museum in Harlem. He had a wonderful big band. And we had kind of semi-regular gigs with that band. Mel Lewis was the drummer. And I was recording for Concord at that time, traveling quite a bit which I still am,…
